newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania prepares for troops amid new violence.
newsitem.headline: Albania prepares for troops amid new violence.

text.p: An advance team of military experts from six countries on Thursday wound up its preparations for the arrival of a multinational security force which aims to secure key harbours and the main airport in anarchic Albania.

"The military experts from the countries sending troops have visited the main areas where the multinational troops will be installed," said Pandeli Ristani, spokesman for the Albanian Defence Ministry.

But as government leaders said they were hopeful the 6,000-strong U.N. backed security force will help restore law and order to the Balkan nation, fresh violence erupted on Thursday after several days of relative calm.

One police officer was killed in the northern town of Skhoder shortly after 9 a.m. when an armed gang drove to the police station and opened fire from their cars. The gun battle in Albania's third largest city lasted for about 10 minutes before the assailants drove away.

It was unclear whether the attack on the Shkoder police station was related to the dismissal of its police chief earlier this week after armed bandits attacked a car carrying Prime Minister Bashkim Fino.
In the southern town of Permet, one security guard was killed and two others injured by a group of gangsters who shot their way into a storage depot they were guarding.
The southern city of Vlore and its 80,000 residents were without water after unknown gunmen shot to pieces the electrical system of the main water pumping station during the night.
Automatic rifle fire was also heard sporadically in Tirana during the day on Thursday.

More than 200 people have been killed and about 700 injured since the uprising began earlier this year when get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes failed and armed rebels took control of the south during an unchecked spasm of looting and banditry.
Army arsenals were looted after soldiers and police abandoned their posts while automatic rifles and weapons were seized by citizens who brandished them on the streets.
A strictly enforced 8 p.m. to 7 a.m. curfew has restored a semblance of order to the capital and surrounding area, but many regions are still considered to be lawless.
The 6,000-strong U.N.-backed security force is due to begin arriving in Albania on Monday.

The Italian news agency ANSA said a small advance unit of Italian troops -- around 20 army pioneers and a group of marines -- would arrive in the port of Durres on Friday to pave the way for the main deployment.
The main force, comprising troops from Italy, France, Spain, Turkey, Greece and Romania, will protect the delivery of emergency food and medical supplies to Albania.
In Tirana, special units of Albanian police have launched operations against gangs in recent days.
Witnesses said about 10 heavily armed and masked officers swooped down on two young men believed to be part of a group that has been firing Kalashnikov rifles into the air at night.
The police began the dawn raid by firing into the air in a show of force before grabbing the young men and beating them in full view of nearby residents. The two were taken away in vans.
Local residents also report that special police troops have stepped up controls inside bars and restaurants in Tirana.
